data.title: Bangkok Theatre Festival stages 103 shows in November
data.description: Bangkok Theatre Festival 2026 brings Thai and international artists to four venues, with interactive productions and selected free performances.

data.title: S.Korean factory owner jailed for anal assault on Thai worker
data.description: A South Korean factory owner who injured an illegal Thai worker by inserting a compressed-air gun nozzle into his anus has been jailed for three years. A charge against his wife was dropped.

data.title: Flooding remains in Bangkok and 22 provinces
data.description: Flooding continues in parts of Bangkok and 22 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were falling on Monday, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation.

data.title: Australia's new Ghost Shark submarines grow some 'teeth'
data.description: SYDNEY - Australia is boosting its undersea warfare capability by equipping its Ghost Shark autonomous submarine with "swarms" of aerial drones and sea mines, its defence ministry said Monday.

data.title: ONE Championship: Akimoto camp alleges illegal knees in Haggerty title defeat
data.description: Japanese challenger Hiroki Akimoto’s camp has renewed its call for a review of his ONE Championship defeat by British champion Jonathan Haggerty, alleging that two illegal knee attacks went unpunished.

data.title: ONE Championship: Nabil challenges Yoza to Muay Thai after ‘boring’ criticism
data.description: Nabil Anane has challenged Yuki Yoza to face him under Muay Thai rules after the Japanese striker criticised their ONE Samurai 4 contest as boring.

data.title: Record El Nino? Depends who's counting
data.description: WASHINGTON - Britain's Met Office says this year's El Nino is "unprecedented." Japan's weather agency has called it the strongest ever observed. US forecasters say it still trails the biggest events in its record books.

data.title: China’s embassy issues fresh Thailand travel alert over kidnappings, job scams
data.description: China's embassy in Thailand has warned citizens to carefully plan their trips and pay extra attention to transport security following a string of high-profile kidnappings targeting Chinese nationals.

data.title: Nations seek reset at UN talks as nature goals off track
data.description: YEREVAN - Nearly 200 nations are gathering in Armenia on Monday for critical negotiations as governments come under pressure to salvage a landmark nature pact whose goals are slipping out of reach.

data.title: Rubio seeks to strengthen US foothold in Central Asia
data.description: SAMARKAND, Uzbekistan - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launches into talks on Monday with key Central Asian states before heading to India on a tour to a region with vast natural resources and China as a key competitor.

data.title: Second day of street clashes in Milan
data.description: MILAN (ITALY) - Youths and police clashed for a second day Sunday in Milan, where mostly black-clad vandals hurled bottles, ransacked stores, and destroyed property around the central Duomo plaza.

data.title: Extraordinary Travel Festival  returns with tales of the road
data.description: The highly-anticipated Extraordinary Travel Festival will return to Bangkok for a third gathering of the world's most accomplished and adventurous travellers, at Ambassador Hotel, Sukhumvit 11, from Thursday to Sunday.

data.title: Your daily horoscope for Oct 19
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on.

data.title: Sarapad Thai  opens store  at QSNCC
data.description: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) recently opened Sarapad Thai, a curated destination bringing together Thai crafts, design, food and gifts through a contemporary lens at its Retail Zone on the ground floor.

data.title: Sharks still in search of first victory
data.description: Chonburi remain without a win this season after a 2-1 home defeat by PT Prachuap in Thai League 1 on Saturday night, despite a change of head coach.

data.title: 2026 Contemporary World Film Series  screens Yoshiyuki Kishi's Sunset Sunrise
data.description: The 2026 Contemporary World Film Series is screening Sunset Sunrise, an award-winning movie from Japan, at TK Park, 8th floor of CentralWorld, Ratchadamri Road, on Sunday at 4pm.

data.title: Molly's milestone
data.description: Molly is an iconic girl character created by Hong Kong artist and designer Kenny Wong in 2006. She is recognised for her blonde hair, big green or blue eyes and signature pout. In 2016, Pop Mart discovered Molly and partnered with Wong to turn Molly into the company's first official Intellectual Property.

data.title: Rail travel to expand in 5 provinces
data.description: The Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) plans to expand rail-based public transport into five regional provinces, aiming to improve connectivity, attract investment and support economic growth beyond Bangkok.

data.title: Ministry eyes extension to B40 promotion train tickets
data.description: The Transport Ministry is considering extending the 40-baht all-day fare scheme for Bangkok's Red and Purple electric train lines beyond its Nov 30 expiry.

data.title: Dept opposes plan to open mine near world heritage site
data.description: A conservation agency in Phetchaburi has opposed a proposed dolomite mine near Kaeng Krachan World Heritage Site, warning of potential harm to wildlife, water resources and local communities.

data.title: Dolphin conservation efforts broaden
data.description: On the shores of Songkhla Lake, the survival of endangered Irrawaddy dolphins is tied to the livelihoods of the people who share their habitat.

data.title: Probe into brazen Korat encroachment steps up
data.description: A probe into the encroachment of more than 189 rai (about 75 acres) of national forest reserves in Nakhon Ratchasima will accelerate after surveys confirmed it was all protected land.

data.title: Nida poll: Interior Ministry seen facing toughest censure grilling
data.description: The Interior Ministry is expected to face the toughest scrutiny in the coming no-confidence debate, according to a Nida Poll survey, with 45% of the respondents believing the opposition has solid evidence against the 18 targeted cabinet ministers.

data.title: Prachin Buri oil leak suspected
data.description: The Pollution Control Department (PCD) is now testing water quality and preparing to contain oil slicks in Prachin Buri after a suspected oil film was detected, amid concerns it could reach the Prachin Buri River.

data.title: Online gambling crackdown  deemed 'ineffective' by ex-MP
data.description: Former Democrat Party MP Sirichoke Sopha has questioned the effectiveness of the Digital Economy and Society (DES) Ministry's crackdown on online gambling, claiming that five major betting websites remain accessible from Thailand despite the ministry's announcement that it had blocked 945,075 links.

data.title: Experts urge use of 'alternative data' for better credit checks
data.description: As Asean's digital economy accelerates, policymakers and financial leaders are turning to alternative data as a tool to broaden access to credit for businesses and individuals excluded from traditional systems.

data.title: Thais eye nature-positive economic model
data.description: Thailand is seeking to reshape its economic model by making sustainability, biodiversity protection and innovation central to national development.

data.title: Two policemen killed in separate attacks
data.description: Two police were killed in separate attacks in the southern border province of Narathiwat.

data.title: Traders in Khlong Chan Flats rebuild after historic floods
data.description: Small business owners in Khlong Chan Flats have reopened their shops after a week of severe flooding, but mounting debts and lost income are driving calls for urgent government assistance.

data.title: World Bank loans $200m
data.description: Thailand has secured US$200 million (6.7 billion baht) in World Bank financing for clean energy and low-carbon cities, turning its International Monetary Fund (IMF)-World Bank annual meetings into economic opportunities for businesses and communities.

data.title: Trump backs ally Netanyahu ahead of Israel's tight election
data.description: JERUSALEM - US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel's close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister's bid to win a new mandate.

data.title: Venezuela opposition alliance reaffirms Nobel laureate Machado as leader
data.description: CARACAS - An alliance of Venezuelan opposition parties on Sunday reaffirmed exiled Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado as its leader, increasing pressure on interim authorities to allow her return.

data.title: Albanian PM refuses to quit as violent protests enter sixth day
data.description: TIRANA (ALBANIA) - Albanian police fired water cannon and tear gas Sunday as violent anti-government protests entered a sixth day and Prime Minister Edi Rama rejected demonstrators' demands that he resign.

data.title: Alberta separatists rally ahead of independence vote
data.description: EDMONTON (CANADA) - Supporters of Alberta's independence from Canada gathered Saturday in the provincial capital to urge residents to vote in favor of holding a future referendum on the issue.

data.title: Ukraine sets Saint Petersburg refinery ablaze in large-scale drone attack
data.description: SAINT PETERSBURG (RUSSIA) - Ukraine hit Saint Petersburg with a large-scale drone attack, causing fires at an oil refinery and depot, Moscow said Sunday, as Kyiv accused Russia of violating Donald Trump's "energy ceasefire" dozens of times and leaving tens of thousands without power.

data.title: Pope addresses crowd in Vatican after cancer surgery
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV addressed thousands of people in St Peter's Square on Sunday, smiling and saying he would resume work "gradually" in his first major public appearance since undergoing lung cancer surgery.

data.title: Flood victims face delays
data.description: Flood victims in Bangkok faced long queues and confusion when seeking compensation on Sunday as registration quotas filled early and residents reported difficulties using the government’s online application.
